name: Recognizing and Fixing Poor Past Window Installations in LA County Homes

mainEntity.name: What are the specific signs of poor past window installations commonly seen in Los Angeles County homes, and how should new installers address them?
mainEntity.text: What are the specific signs of poor past window installations commonly seen in Los Angeles County homes, and how should new installers address them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many Los Angeles County homes have gone through at least one window replacement, and not all were done correctly. Telltale signs of poor past installations include recurring diagonal stucco cracks from window corners, interior wall or ceiling staining below windows after rain, and drafts or cold spots despite having dual-pane glass. You might also notice sashes that bind or do not fully close, or large, uneven beads of caulk applied as repeated band-aid fixes. When planning a new project, ask the installer to investigate beyond the surface. They should look for signs of water intrusion, such as soft or darkened wood at sills, rusted fasteners, or moldy drywall. Stucco cracks near windows may indicate movement or improper integration of flashing and lath with the original wall assembly. A thorough contractor will propose solutions that address root causes: improving flashing details, adding sill pans, properly sealing to housewrap or building paper, and repairing damaged framing. In some cases, they may recommend switching from retrofit to full-frame replacement in problem areas. Request that the installer document any discovered damage with photos and explain how their new installation method will prevent the same issues from recurring, not just swap in new windows.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common signs of poor past window installations in Los Angeles County include recurring stucco cracks at corners, interior staining below sills after rain, drafty frames, binding sashes, and excessive caulking repairs. New installers should inspect framing, flashing, and moisture damage, then correct underlying issues instead of just replacing units in the same way.
